sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `goose`
- Canonical name: Goose, stewarded by AAIF in the Linux Foundation ecosystem and founded by Block (`claim-goose-w2-identity`)
- Current status: active repository; latest checked stable release v1.45.0 (`claim-goose-w2-status`, `claim-goose-w2-version`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-10

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: a general-purpose local agent runtime with CLI, Desktop, provider choice, MCP extensions, recipes, and user-hosted remote options (`claim-goose-w2-primary-type`, `claim-goose-w2-unique`).
- What it is not: no Goose-managed cloud workspace or current native mobile app was established (`claim-goose-w2-not-for`). The retired iOS tunnel and archived Android app are historical surfaces only (`claim-goose-w2-surface-mobile-retired`).

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` (`claim-goose-w2-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: Goose owns direct-provider loops; an external ACP agent owns delegated tool execution in ACP-provider mode (`claim-goose-w2-loop-ownership`).
- Architecture: local Desktop/CLI runtime or user-run `goose serve` on a local or remote machine (`claim-goose-w2-execution`, `claim-goose-w2-remote-auth`).

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-goose-cli`, `surface-goose-desktop-local`, `surface-goose-acp-stdio`, `surface-goose-serve`, `surface-goose-desktop-remote-backend`, `surface-goose-vscode`, `surface-goose-zed-acp`, `surface-goose-telegram`, `surface-goose-terminal-integration`, `surface-goose-private-network`, `surface-goose-mobile-tunnel-retired`, `surface-goose-mobile-android-archived`, `surface-goose-tui-retired`.
- Execution location: same-device by default or user-controlled remote machine for `goose serve`; no Goose-managed execution service was established (`claim-goose-w2-execution`, `claim-goose-w2-not-for`).

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: direct APIs, local models, custom providers, ACP agents, and provider-specific routes are documented; general automatic fallback is unknown (`claim-goose-w2-provider-auth`, `claim-goose-w2-custom-providers`).
- Auth strategy: API keys, system keyring, environment overrides, and plain-file fallback (`claim-goose-w2-auth-modes`).
- Provider support: the README claims 15+ providers, direct APIs, and ACP subscription reuse; the provider guide separately establishes local Ollama, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and custom providers (`claim-goose-w2-provider-auth`, `claim-goose-w2-custom-providers`). Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Pi compatibility paths remain separate (`claim-goose-w2-acp-claude`, `claim-goose-w2-acp-codex`, `claim-goose-w2-gemini-cli-provider`, `claim-goose-w2-acp-pi`).

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: native sessions persist locally; provider/model limits remain route-specific (`claim-goose-w2-session-context`).
- Memory: optional Memory and Chat Recall extensions provide project/global memory and prior-session search (`claim-goose-w2-memory-compaction`).
- Compaction: automatic compaction near 80 percent, a configurable threshold, and manual `/compact` are documented separately (`claim-goose-w2-compaction`).
- Session behavior: native resume/fork/export differs from ACP-provider new-session-only behavior (`claim-goose-w2-session-context`, `claim-goose-w2-acp-session-limit`).

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: extension and local tools run under Goose permission modes; default whole-runtime isolation is not established (`claim-goose-w2-security`).
- Extensions: Goose connects to 70+ MCP extensions (`claim-goose-w2-extension-stack`).
- MCP: Goose connects to 70+ extensions via MCP (`claim-goose-w2-extension-stack`).
- Skills: `unknown`.
- Hooks: `unknown`.
- APIs: ACP stdio and HTTP/WebSocket `goose serve` (`claim-goose-w2-surface-api`).

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: temporary subagents and subrecipes (`claim-goose-w2-orchestration`).
- Parallelism: parallel subagents (`claim-goose-w2-orchestration`).

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: maintainers recommend VM/container isolation for risky use; no default whole-runtime sandbox was established (`claim-goose-w2-security-caution`).
- Permissions: Autonomous is default; Manual, Smart, Chat Only, and per-tool controls are available (`claim-goose-w2-security`).
- Security: remote server secret, TLS, origin policy, and certificate pinning are split across transport code and the remote guide (`claim-goose-w2-remote-auth`, `claim-goose-w2-certificate-pinning`).
- Data path: command history, session records, logs, and LLM request logs stay on local disk; provider retention remains unknown in this repaired claim set (`claim-goose-w2-data-path`).

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Local: `surface-goose-cli`, `surface-goose-desktop-local`, `surface-goose-terminal-integration` (`claim-goose-w2-surface-cli-desktop`, `claim-goose-w2-surface-terminal-integration`).
  - APIs: `surface-goose-acp-stdio`, `surface-goose-serve` (`claim-goose-w2-surface-api`).
  - Remote client: `surface-goose-desktop-remote-backend` (`claim-goose-w2-surface-remote-desktop`).
  - IDE: `surface-goose-vscode`, `surface-goose-zed-acp` (`claim-goose-w2-surface-ide`).
  - Messaging: `surface-goose-telegram` (`claim-goose-w2-surface-telegram`).
  - Generic private network: `surface-goose-private-network` (`claim-goose-w2-surface-private-network`).
  - Historical unsupported routes: `surface-goose-mobile-tunnel-retired`, `surface-goose-mobile-android-archived`, `surface-goose-tui-retired` (`claim-goose-w2-surface-mobile-retired`, `claim-goose-w2-surface-tui-retired`).
- Remote behavior: Desktop connects directly to a separately started user-run backend; VPN/tailnet reachability is generic infrastructure; no vendor relay is established (`claim-goose-w2-surface-remote-desktop`, `claim-goose-w2-surface-private-network`, `claim-goose-w2-not-for`).
- Mobile behavior: current native mobile and mobile web remain unknown; old iOS and Android routes are retired or archived. Telegram is a separate messaging gateway (`claim-goose-w2-surface-mobile-retired`, `claim-goose-w2-surface-telegram`).
- Background behavior: `unknown`.

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: Goose-owned subscription and hosted-service pricing remain unknown; provider costs are external (`claim-goose-w2-pricing`).
- License: code/specifications Apache-2.0; non-spec documentation CC BY 4.0 (`claim-goose-w2-license`).
- Maintenance: active repository and v1.45.0 release (`claim-goose-w2-status`, `claim-goose-w2-version`).
- Lock-in: broad direct, local, custom, and ACP provider paths exist, but each provider and subscription route has its own auth policy (`claim-goose-w2-provider-auth`, `claim-goose-w2-custom-providers`, `claim-goose-w2-auth-modes`).

sections.heading: Lineage and compatibility edges
sections.body:
- Lineage claims: no Goose fork or shared-runtime lineage with selected Wave 2 products was established.
- Relationship edges:
  - `goose --connects_via--> claude-code`; `goose --reuses_auth_from--> claude-code` (`claim-goose-w2-acp-claude`).
  - `goose --connects_via--> codex-family`; `goose --reuses_auth_from--> codex-family` (`claim-goose-w2-acp-codex`).
  - `goose --orchestrates--> codex-family` (`claim-goose-w2-codex-subagent`).
  - `goose --connects_via--> gemini-cli`; `goose --reuses_auth_from--> gemini-cli` (`claim-goose-w2-gemini-cli-provider`).
  - `goose --connects_via--> pi`; `goose --reuses_auth_from--> pi` (`claim-goose-w2-acp-pi`).

sections.heading: Closest substitutes, partial substitutes, same-lineage relatives, often-confused products, and complements
sections.body:
- Comparison neighborhood IDs: `unknown`; no new Wave 2 neighborhood row was emitted.
- Substitutes: `unknown`
- Partial substitutes: `unknown`
- Same-lineage relatives: `unknown`
- Often-confused products: deprecated CLI-provider routes and current ACP-provider routes are not one support state (`claim-goose-w2-gemini-cli-provider`, `claim-goose-w2-acp-claude`, `claim-goose-w2-acp-codex`).
- Complements: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Pi have evidence-backed compatibility edges, but no neighborhood memberships were asserted.

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: general-purpose local runtime with native Desktop/CLI, broad providers, local models, and MCP extensions (`claim-goose-w2-unique`).
- Meaningful drawbacks: autonomous default and local permission risk (`claim-goose-w2-drawback`); extension/provider trust (`claim-goose-w2-security-caution`); experimental or retired routes (`claim-goose-w2-surface-ide`, `claim-goose-w2-surface-telegram`, `claim-goose-w2-surface-mobile-retired`, `claim-goose-w2-surface-tui-retired`); deprecated pass-through providers (`claim-goose-w2-gemini-cli-provider`); and ACP resume/fork limits (`claim-goose-w2-acp-session-limit`).
- Best fit: official positioning addresses developers and technical users wanting a local, extensible, provider-flexible agent for code and non-code tasks (`claim-goose-w2-intended-user`). This is not a recommendation.
- Not-for: verified Goose-managed cloud or current native-mobile requirements (`claim-goose-w2-not-for`).
